summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of multiple coronary stents was admitted for evaluation of recurrent chest pain. The pain, occurring at rest and relieved by nitroglycerin, was consistent with unstable angina. Cardiac catheterization revealed a 90% stenosis in the distal right coronary artery, where a drug-eluting stent was successfully placed. The patient tolerated the procedure well, with resolution of symptoms. He also had a minimally displaced right patellar fracture from a recent fall, managed non-operatively with bracing. He received dialysis during admission, and his medications were continued without complications. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up with cardiology, primary care, and orthopedics, and to maintain a heart-healthy diet and daily weight monitoring.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with unstable angina pectoris
Other fracture of right patella, initial encounter for closed fracture
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft
